title: The doubling flow, for every step — 16 machine-checked theorems and how they are bound
description:
The doubling flow, for every step. 16 machine-checked theorems from the Lean 4 source file src/proof/flow.lean, by Tsvetan Rouschev, licensed CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Lean 4 is a proof checker: a theorem it accepts has been checked by its kernel, not argued in prose. All are proved for every value, on the standard axioms only (propext, Quot.sound; the verifier refuses any other). Every theorem listed is sealed live in the deposit's ledger, where a withdrawal is marked in place; 63 earlier rows removed on 2026-08-09 are listed in src/proof/revoked.json.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used here in a precise, non-quantum sense: theorems are bound when they derive from shared definitions (section 1), when their files import one another (section 2), and when their content-addressed receipts fold into one address that changes if any one of them changes (section 3). It is correlation by derivation; no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 6 definitions are used by two or more theorems, binding 64 pairs; the theorems fall into 2 strands, the largest of 11. Most binding: ringSum (10), orbit (5), ringNext (4), ringPrev (2), burgersSkew3 (2), ringLap (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: index.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 2 files: src/proof/flow.lean, src/proof/index.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 16 sealed receipts fold to 37b2ea68-1622-81a3-b8c7-82bd3b32bc2b. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed when this record was generated. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (1, 3, 5, 8, 8, 7, 6). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs counted from this cluster's theorems' seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: generated.lean (4 observed, 1.78 expected, lift 2.24), elementary.lean (12 observed, 5.49 expected, lift 2.19), demand.lean (3 observed, 1.51 expected, lift 1.99). A best lift is the largest of about 32 small ratios, so chance alone gives a typical best lift of 2.73 here (the median over 200 seeded reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to); one at least as high as this cluster's arose in 88.0% of them — consistent with chance. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.79; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.58. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). These figures are as of commit 019737516dc4 (2026-09-15), over 817 points; a new seal anywhere moves them.

Prior art. 2⁶ = 64 ≡ 1 (mod 9), so the powers of two modulo 9 repeat with period six — Euler's theorem for φ(9) = 6, and the order of 2 in U(9), both textbook. Credited, and bounded: what this file adds is the kernel proof that the flow used by navier_stokes_flow_is_bounded stays bounded at EVERY step, not only at the 48 that theorem checks. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json (main branch). No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. the_doubling_flow_repeats_every_six_steps — ∀ k : Nat, orbit (k + 6) = orbit k record
  2. the_doubling_flow_is_its_first_six_steps — ∀ k : Nat, orbit k = orbit (k % 6) record
  3. navier_stokes_flow_is_bounded_for_every_step — ∀ k : Nat, orbit k < 9 ∧ span.contains (orbit k) = true record
  4. the_reverse_flow_undoes_every_step — ∀ k : Nat, orbit (k + 1) * 5 % 9 = orbit k record
  5. every_state_of_the_flow_returns_within_six_steps — ∀ k s : Nat, ∃ j, j < 6 ∧ orbit (k + j) = orbit s record
  6. a_ring_sum_splits_over_a_sum — ∀ (f g : Nat → Int) (n : Nat), ringSum (fun i => f i + g i) n = ringSum f n + ringSum g n record
  7. a_ring_sum_of_negatives_is_the_negated_sum — ∀ (f : Nat → Int) (n : Nat), ringSum (fun i => - f i) n = - ringSum f n record
  8. ring_sums_agree_where_their_terms_agree — ∀ (f g : Nat → Int) (n : Nat), (∀ i, i < n → f i = g i) → ringSum f n = ringSum g n record
  9. a_ring_sum_peels_its_first_term — ∀ (f : Nat → Int) (n : Nat), ringSum f (n + 1) = f 0 + ringSum (fun i => f (i + 1)) n record
  10. a_cyclic_sum_is_unchanged_by_one_step_of_rotation — ∀ (N : Nat) (f : Nat → Int), 0 < N → ringSum (fun i => f (ringNext N i)) N = ringSum f N record
  11. the_site_before_the_next_is_the_site — ∀ N i : Nat, i < N → ringPrev N (ringNext N i) = i record
  12. a_bond_sum_reads_the_same_from_either_end — ∀ (N : Nat) (F : Nat → Nat → Int), 0 < N → ringSum (fun i => F (ringPrev N i) i) N = ringSum (fun i => F i (ringNext N i)) N record
  13. the_skew_symmetric_burgers_term_does_no_work_on_every_ring — ∀ (N : Nat) (u : Nat → Int), 0 < N → ringSum (fun i => u i * burgersSkew3 N u i) N = 0 record
  14. the_discrete_laplacian_dissipates_exactly_the_squared_differences — ∀ (N : Nat) (u : Nat → Int), 0 < N → ringSum (fun i => u i * ringLap N u i) N = - ringSum (fun i => (u (ringNext N i) - u i) * (u (ringNext N i) - u i)) N record
  15. a_sum_of_squares_is_never_negative — ∀ (f : Nat → Int) (n : Nat), 0 ≤ ringSum (fun i => f i * f i) n record
  16. the_discrete_energy_never_increases_on_every_ring — ∀ (N : Nat) (u : Nat → Int) (ν : Int), 0 < N → 0 ≤ ν → ringSum (fun i => u i * (3 * ν * ringLap N u i - burgersSkew3 N u i)) N ≤ 0 record
